vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security updates - immediate, high priority. This must be the top-level vulnerabilityAlerts object, which applies only to updates that fix a known vulnerability: as a packageRule matching every package it labelled every update security/urgent, titled it fix(security) and dropped its schedule and release-age wait (PR #154 was a plain Go minor bump).

schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Testing libraries - safe automerge for patches

GitHub Actions - major updates: automerge after a 14-day soak once CI passes. Actions are SHA-pinned and gated by the full PR CI (lint/test/e2e/build); only release.yml-exclusive actions aren't exercised by PR CI, so watch the first release after a docker/* action major.

Dockerfile's golang base image tag moves with this repo's go.mod, not on its own datasource/schedule (e.g. PR #151). Disable the built-in dockerfile manager for it - the xp-provider-gen-go-version customManager below tracks it together with go.mod, in one PR.

The `go` directive of this repo's go.mod moves with the Dockerfile's golang tag: the xp-provider-gen-go-version customManager below bumps both. Disable the gomod manager's own proposal for it (it would bump go.mod alone).

Both Go versions share one rule, so each gets one release-age wait: the generator's (go.mod and the Dockerfile tag, one PR) and the generated providers' (go_version alone). Without it the provider-framework rule (matched by file name) took go_version into its group with a 7-day wait while the Dockerfile tag went alone with none (#154, #157). Patches get their own PR (separateMinorPatch), so declining a Go minor bump can never also block a security patch on the current minor.

Generated-provider framework deps (pkg/versions/dependencies.yaml) - bump together so crossplane-runtime, crossplane/apis, controller-runtime, and k8s.io/* stay mutually compatible (individual bumps break the e2e)

Never propose upjet/v2 v2.4.0 or older: released v2.4.0 imports crossplane-runtime/v2/apis/common/v1, which crossplane-runtime removed in its own v2.4.0, so make generate fails in a scaffolded upjet provider. upjet was once pinned to a post-v2.4.0 pseudo-version for this, and with rollbackPrs enabled Renovate proposed v2.4.0 as a 'rollback' (PRs #134, #152). The pin is a release (v2.5.1) now; the floor stays so a rollback can never be proposed again.
The build submodule pin moves on its own: build has no releases, and a new pin changes what every new scaffold gets, so it lands alone, not inside the crossplane packages group.

Don't track crossplane-tools in pkg/versions/dependencies.yaml: the repo has no tags, so its pin can only be a pseudo-version, and the go datasource behind the regex manager has no releases to match it against ('Can't find version matching ...' on the dashboard). Tracking the commit digest instead would not work either - Renovate would swap the 12-character hash but not the timestamp in front of it, and Go rejects a pseudo-version whose timestamp does not match the commit. Bump it by hand: `go list -m github.com/crossplane/crossplane-tools@<commit>` prints the right pseudo-version. Never go below the 2026-07-15 build - older angryjet silently generates no methodsets for the core/v2 types, and the scaffolded provider then fails go build.

customManagers.description: Track generated-provider dependency versions in pkg/versions/dependencies.yaml

Track the Go this repo is built with as ONE dependency across the Dockerfile's golang base image tag and the `go` directive of go.mod, so a bump proposes both together in a single PR - never one alone (that drift broke the image build five times in September). It is independent of the Go generated providers declare, tracked next.
Track the Go language version generated providers declare, pkg/versions/dependencies.yaml's go_version, alone. scripts/check-go-version fails CI if it falls below what a pinned dependency requires.

Track golangci-lint through pkg/versions/dependencies.yaml's golangci_lint_version, the one place it is pinned: this repo's Makefile and lint.yml read it, and both flavors' generated make fragment render it.
Track the crossplane/build commit generated providers pin their build submodule at, through pkg/versions/dependencies.yaml's build_ref, as a digest of build's main branch.

Track the git-cliff release version release.yml installs from GitHub releases as a pinned binary (deliberately not orhun/git-cliff-action, see release.yml's comment). The action's own `uses:` SHA is tracked separately by helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests.

Track the GoReleaser version goreleaser-action's `version:` input pins in release.yml - a floating input Renovate does not follow on its own (the action's `uses:` SHA is tracked separately by helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests).
